attempts.rationale: Robust aggregator for unstable rankings and correlated error groups; median is insensitive to a few outlier models in the pool.

Robust aggregator alternative to median: averages the middle 60% of 19 models, more informative than a single median point while still trimming the worst forecasts. Tests whether the middle of the distribution carries more signal than the exact median.

Smooth error-proportional weighting to complement the hard-trim robust aggregators already tested; with unstable rankings this gives graded influence rather than binary inclusion, potentially reducing variance from the 7 correlated-error groups.

DBA optimizes linear weights over the full pool, exploiting complementary errors across 7 correlation groups. Different kind from aggregation (median/trimmed) or formula-based (softmax) weighting; suited to unstable rankings where the best mix shifts across windows.

Per-horizon top-k mean exploits the unstable ranking: different models dominate different horizons, so a global weight is suboptimal. Top-5 per step on SMAPE captures the best local model at each step while averaging for robustness.

Meta-model weights use cross-series knowledge to assign weights, a different information source than per-window error. With strong trend (0.90) and non-stationary series, cross-series pattern matching may complement the per-horizon approach that currently leads.
Simple 1/error weighting as a contrast to per-horizon topk (leader) and near-uniform softmax (runner-up); motivated by unstable cross-window rankings where complex weight estimation is high-variance.
Restricted top-7 SMAPE pool with flat mean: tests whether removing the weakest models and dropping per-horizon complexity improves robustness under unstable rankings (tau=-0.255).

Extreme per-horizon: pick single best model at each step. Tests whether unstable rankings (tau=-0.255) benefit from one-hot selection vs topk-mean averaging. Different kind from leader's topk_per_horizon.

Forward selection picked 3 diverse models (NaiveMovingAverage, FT_rf, THETA) from different correlation groups; tests whether Caruana-style selection beats uniform/inverse-error weighting on this strongly-trended, unstable-ranking series.

Unweighted mean across all 19 models: maximum diversity, no weight-estimation variance, robust to unstable rankings (tau=-0.255) and 7 correlated error groups. Different kind from all 5 weighted schemes already tested.
